782	#### Filter by tool name and arguments with the `if` field
783	
784	The `if` field uses [permission rule syntax](/docs/en/permissions) to filter hooks by tool name and arguments together, so the hook process only spawns when the tool call matches. This goes beyond `matcher`, which filters at the group level by tool name only.
785	
786	For example, this configuration runs a hook only when Claude uses `git` commands rather than all Bash commands:
787	
788	```json theme={null}
789	{
790	  "hooks": {
791	    "PreToolUse": [
792	      {
793	        "matcher": "Bash",
794	        "hooks": [
795	          {
796	            "type": "command",
797	            "if": "Bash(git *)",
798	            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/check-git-policy.sh"
799	          }
800	        ]
801	      }
802	    ]
803	  }
804	}
805	```
806	
807	Whether your hook command runs depends on the shape of your `if` pattern and the Bash command Claude is invoking:
808	
809	| `if` pattern       | Bash command           | Hook runs? | Why                                                                                                 |
810	| :----------------- | :--------------------- | :--------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
811	| `Bash(git *)`      | `git push`             | yes        | command name matches                                                                                |
812	| `Bash(git *)`      | `npm test && git push` | yes        | each subcommand is checked; `git push` matches                                                      |
813	| `Bash(git *)`      | `echo $(git log)`      | yes        | commands inside `$()` and backticks are checked; `git log` matches                                  |
814	| `Bash(git *)`      | `echo $(date)`         | no         | no subcommand matches `git *`                                                                       |
815	| `Bash(git push *)` | `echo $(date)`         | yes        | patterns that specify more than the command name run the hook anyway on `$()`, backticks, or `$VAR` |
816	
817	When Claude Code can't determine which commands the Bash input runs, it runs your hook regardless of the pattern. The [Bash matching table](/docs/en/hooks#bash-if-matching) covers the command shapes Claude Code can and can't narrow by subcommand. Because the filter is best-effort, use the [permission system](/docs/en/permissions) rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny.
818	
819	The `if` field accepts the same patterns as permission rules: `"Bash(git *)"`, `"Edit(*.ts)"`, and so on. To match multiple tool names, use separate handlers each with its own `if` value, or match at the `matcher` level where pipe alternation is supported.
820	
821	`if` only works on tool events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, and `PermissionDenied`. Adding it to any other event prevents the hook from running.
822	
823	### Configure hook location
824	
825	Where you add a hook determines its scope:
826	
827	| Location                                 | Scope                                                                                                                     | Shareable                                             |
828	| :--------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------- |
829	| `~/.claude/settings.json`                | All your projects                                                                                                         | No, local to your machine                             |
830	| `.claude/settings.json`                  | Single project                                                                                                            | Yes, can be committed to the repo                     |
831	| `.claude/settings.local.json`            | Single project                                                                                                            | No, gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting to it |
832	| Managed policy settings                  | Organization-wide                                                                                                         | Yes, admin-controlled                                 |
833	| [Plugin](/docs/en/plugins) `hooks/hooks.json` | When plugin is enabled                                                                                                    | Yes, bundled with the plugin                          |
834	| [Skill](/docs/en/skills) frontmatter          | The rest of the session once the skill is invoked. See [Hooks in skills and agents](/docs/en/hooks#hooks-in-skills-and-agents) | Yes, defined in the skill file                        |
835	| [Subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) frontmatter   | While that subagent is running                                                                                            | Yes, defined in the subagent file                     |
836	
837	Run [`/hooks`](/docs/en/hooks#the-%2Fhooks-menu) in Claude Code to browse all configured hooks grouped by event.
838	
839	To disable hooks, set `"disableAllHooks": true` in your settings file. Claude Code reads the value left after [settings precedence](/docs/en/hooks#disable-or-remove-hooks) applies, so a project's settings file can override yours. Hooks configured in managed settings still run unless `disableAllHooks` is also set there. For the full reach of each level, see [`disableAllHooks`](/docs/en/settings-reference#disableallhooks).
840	
841	If you edit settings files directly while Claude Code is running, the file watcher normally picks up hook changes automatically.
842	
843	## Prompt-based hooks
844	
845	For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, use `type: "prompt"` hooks. Instead of running a shell command, Claude Code sends your prompt and the hook's input data to a Claude model, Haiku by default, to make the decision. You can specify a different model with the `model` field if you need more capability.
846	
847	The model's only job is to return its decision as JSON:
848	
849	* `"ok": true`: the action proceeds
850	* `"ok": false`: what happens depends on the event:
851	  * `Stop` and `SubagentStop`: the `reason` is fed back to Claude so it keeps working, unless the response also sets `"impossible": true` to mark the condition as one that can never be satisfied, in which case Claude Code allows the stop and the turn ends
852	  * `PreToolUse`: the tool call is denied; by default the turn ends and the deny `reason` appears in the chat as a warning line. Set `continueOnBlock: true` on the hook to instead return the `reason` to Claude as the tool error, so it can adjust and continue. Before v2.1.210, the deny `reason` was returned to Claude as the tool error and the turn continued
853	  * `PostToolUse`: by default the turn ends and the `reason` appears in the chat as a warning line. Set `continueOnBlock: true` to feed the `reason` back to Claude and continue the turn instead
854	  * `PostToolBatch`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `UserPromptExpansion`: the turn ends and the `reason` appears in the chat as a warning line
855	
856	This example uses a `Stop` hook to ask the model whether all requested tasks are complete. If the model returns `"ok": false` because the condition isn't met yet, Claude keeps working and uses the `reason` as its next instruction:
857	
858	```json theme={null}
859	{
860	  "hooks": {
861	    "Stop": [
862	      {
863	        "hooks": [
864	          {
865	            "type": "prompt",
866	            "prompt": "Check if all tasks are complete. If not, respond with {\"ok\": false, \"reason\": \"what remains to be done\"}."
867	          }
868	        ]
869	      }
870	    ]
871	  }
872	}
873	```
874	
875	For full configuration options, see [Prompt-based hooks](/docs/en/hooks#prompt-based-hooks) in the reference.
876	
877	## Agent-based hooks
878	
879	<Warning>
880	  Agent hooks are experimental. Behavior and configuration may change in future releases. For production workflows, prefer [command hooks](/docs/en/hooks#command-hook-fields).
881	</Warning>
882	
883	When verification requires inspecting files or running commands, use `type: "agent"` hooks. Unlike prompt hooks, which make a single LLM call, agent hooks spawn a subagent that can read files, search code, and use other tools to verify conditions before returning a decision.
884	
885	Agent hooks use the `"ok"` / `"reason"` response format with a longer default timeout of 60 seconds and up to 50 tool-use turns. They don't support the prompt-hook `impossible` field. On `ok: false`, Claude Code handles an agent hook the way it handles a prompt hook with `continueOnBlock: true` on the same event, so on `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` the turn continues; agent hooks have no `continueOnBlock` field. See [agent hook configuration](/docs/en/hooks#agent-hook-configuration) for the fields, including the `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder that Claude Code replaces with the hook's JSON input.
886	
887	This example verifies that tests pass before allowing Claude to stop:
888	
889	```json theme={null}
890	{
891	  "hooks": {
892	    "Stop": [
893	      {
894	        "hooks": [
895	          {
896	            "type": "agent",
897	            "prompt": "Verify that all unit tests pass. Run the test suite and check the results. $ARGUMENTS",
898	            "timeout": 120
899	          }
900	        ]
901	      }
902	    ]
903	  }
904	}
905	```
906	
907	Use prompt hooks when the hook input data alone is enough to make a decision. Use agent hooks when you need to verify something against the actual state of the codebase.
908	
909	For full configuration options, see [Agent-based hooks](/docs/en/hooks#agent-based-hooks) in the reference.
910	
911	## HTTP hooks
912	
913	Use `type: "http"` hooks to POST event data to an HTTP endpoint instead of running a shell command. The endpoint receives the same JSON that a command hook would receive on stdin, and returns results through the HTTP response body using the same JSON format.
914	
915	HTTP hooks are useful when you want a web server, cloud function, or external service to handle hook logic: for example, a shared audit service that logs tool use events across a team.
916	
917	This example posts every tool use to a local logging service:
918	
919	```json theme={null}
920	{
921	  "hooks": {
922	    "PostToolUse": [
923	      {
924	        "hooks": [
925	          {
926	            "type": "http",
927	            "url": "http://localhost:8080/hooks/tool-use",
928	            "headers": {
929	              "Authorization": "Bearer $MY_TOKEN"
930	            },
931	            "allowedEnvVars": ["MY_TOKEN"]
932	          }
933	        ]
934	      }
935	    ]
936	  }
937	}
938	```
939	
940	The endpoint should return a JSON response body using the same [output format](/docs/en/hooks#json-output) as command hooks. To block a tool call, return a 2xx response with the appropriate `hookSpecificOutput` fields. HTTP status codes alone can't block actions.
941	
942	Header values support environment variable interpolation using `$VAR_NAME` or `${VAR_NAME}` syntax. Only variables listed in the `allowedEnvVars` array are resolved; all other `$VAR` references remain empty.
943	
944	For full configuration options and response handling, see [HTTP hooks](/docs/en/hooks#http-hook-fields) in the reference.
945	
946	## Limitations and troubleshooting
947	
948	### Limitations
949	
950	Keep these constraints in mind when designing hooks:
951	
952	* Command hooks communicate through stdout, stderr, and exit codes only. They can't trigger `/` commands or tool calls. Text returned via `additionalContext` is injected as a system reminder that Claude reads as plain text. HTTP hooks communicate through the response body instead.
953	* Hook timeouts vary by type. Override per hook with the `timeout` field in seconds.
954	  * `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`: 10 minutes. Claude Code lowers this default to 30 seconds for `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreModelSwitch`, and `PostModelSwitch` hooks, and to 10 seconds for `MessageDisplay`.
955	  * `prompt`: 30 seconds.
956	  * `agent`: 60 seconds.
957	  * [`SessionEnd`](/docs/en/hooks#sessionend) hooks of any type share a 1.5-second budget. If your settings set a longer per-hook `timeout`, Claude Code raises the budget to match, up to 60 seconds.
958	* `PostToolUse` hooks can't undo actions since the tool has already executed.
959	* `PermissionRequest` hooks fire when Claude Code is about to ask you for permission.
960	  * In [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag, that prompt only exists when the Agent SDK's [`canUseTool` callback](/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions) supplies it. In plain `-p` runs or with `--permission-prompt-tool`, use `PreToolUse` hooks for automated permission decisions instead.
961	  * Background subagents can't show a prompt in non-interactive mode. Claude Code still runs the hooks for their tool calls, and if no hook returns a decision, it denies the call. In an interactive session, background subagent prompts surface in your main session and the hooks fire as usual.
962	* `Stop` hooks fire whenever Claude finishes responding, not only at task completion. They don't fire on user interrupts. API errors fire [StopFailure](/docs/en/hooks#stopfailure) instead.
963	* When multiple `PreToolUse` hooks return [`updatedInput`](/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse) to rewrite a tool's arguments, the last one to finish takes effect. Since hooks run in parallel, the order is non-deterministic. Avoid having more than one hook modify the same tool's input.
964	
965	### Hooks and permission modes
966	
967	`PreToolUse` hooks fire before any permission-mode check, in every [permission mode](/docs/en/permission-modes), including `dontAsk`. A hook that returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` blocks the tool even in `bypassPermissions` mode or with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. This lets you enforce policy that users can't bypass by changing their permission mode.
968	
969	The reverse is not true: a hook returning `"allow"` doesn't bypass deny rules from settings, and it can't suppress the prompt for MCP tools marked [`requiresUserInteraction`](/docs/en/mcp#require-approval-for-a-specific-tool) or for connector tools [your organization set to `ask`](/docs/en/mcp#organization-controls-on-connector-tools) in sessions where that setting reaches Claude Code. Hooks can tighten restrictions but not loosen them past what permission rules allow.
970	
971	### Hook not firing
972	
973	The hook is configured but never executes.
974	
975	* Run `/hooks` and confirm the hook appears under the correct event
976	* Check that the matcher pattern matches the tool name exactly. Matchers are case-sensitive
977	* Verify you're triggering the right event type: `PreToolUse` fires before tool execution, `PostToolUse` fires after. A `PermissionRequest` hook fires when Claude Code is about to ask you for permission; see the [limitations](#limitations) for the non-interactive cases
978	
979	### Hook error in output
980	
981	You see a message like "PreToolUse hook error: ..." in the transcript.
982	
983	* Your script exited with a non-zero code unexpectedly. Test it manually by piping sample JSON:
984	  ```bash theme={null}
985	  echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | ./my-hook.sh
986	  echo $?  # Check the exit code
987	  ```
988	* If you see "command not found", use absolute paths or `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` to reference scripts. To avoid shell quoting entirely, add `"args": []` to switch to [exec form](/docs/en/hooks#exec-form-and-shell-form), which spawns the script directly without a shell
989	* If you see "jq: command not found", install `jq` or use Python/Node.js for JSON parsing
990	* If the notice shows a JSON validation message, your hook's stdout parsed as JSON but failed schema validation. If it shows a JSON parse message, the stdout looked like a JSON object but wasn't valid JSON. Both happen even on exit 0.
991	
992	  To fix a parse failure, build the payload with a JSON encoder such as `jq` instead of string concatenation, so quotes and backslashes inside values are escaped. The reference's [Exit code output](/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output) section covers the exit-code and JSON combinations
993	* If the script isn't running at all, make it executable: `chmod +x ./my-hook.sh`
994	
995	### `/hooks` shows no hooks configured
996	
997	You edited a settings file but the hooks don't appear in the menu.
998	
999	* File edits are normally picked up automatically. If they haven't appeared after a few seconds, the file watcher may have missed the change: restart your session to force a reload.
1000	* Verify your JSON is valid: trailing commas and comments aren't allowed
1001	* Confirm the settings file is in the correct location: `.claude/settings.json` for project hooks, `~/.claude/settings.json` for global hooks
1002	
1003	### Stop hook hits the block cap
1004	
1005	Claude keeps working instead of stopping, then ends the turn with a warning that the Stop hook blocked too many consecutive times.
1006	
1007	Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row without progress. Your hook script needs to check whether it already triggered a continuation. Parse the `stop_hook_active` field from the JSON input and exit early if it's `true`:
1008	
1009	```bash theme={null}
1010	#!/bin/bash
1011	INPUT=$(cat)
1012	if [ "$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then
1013	  exit 0  # Allow Claude to stop
1014	fi
1015	# ... rest of your hook logic
1016	```
1017	
1018	If your hook legitimately needs more than eight iterations to converge, raise the cap with [`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`](/docs/en/env-vars).
1019	
1020	### Hook JSON has no effect
1021	
1022	Your hook prints valid JSON, but the decision doesn't take effect and no error appears in the transcript. Check which cause applies:
1023	
1024	* **Extra output before the JSON**: something else writes to stdout first, usually an unconditional `echo` in your shell profile, so the output no longer starts with `{` and Claude Code doesn't parse it as JSON. The cause and fix follow this list.
1025	* **A field at the wrong level**: compare each field's placement against the [JSON output](/docs/en/hooks#json-output) format. For example, `permissionDecision` belongs inside `hookSpecificOutput`, not at the top level.
1026	
1027	When Claude Code runs a shell-form command hook, one without `args`, it spawns `sh -c` on macOS and Linux, Git Bash on Windows, or PowerShell when Git Bash isn't installed by default. This shell is non-interactive, but Git Bash and some configurations, such as `BASH_ENV` pointing at `~/.bashrc`, still source your profile. If that profile contains unconditional `echo` statements, the output gets prepended to your hook's JSON:
1028	
1029	```text theme={null}
1030	Shell ready on arm64
1031	{"decision": "block", "reason": "Not allowed"}
1032	```
1033	
1034	The combined output no longer starts with `{`, so Claude Code treats all of stdout as plain text and ignores the JSON. On exit 0 nothing is reported in the transcript; the parse attempt is recorded only in the [debug log](/docs/en/hooks#debug-hooks). To fix this, wrap echo statements in your shell profile so they only run in interactive shells:
1035	
1036	```bash theme={null}
1037	# In ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
1038	if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then
1039	  echo "Shell ready"
1040	fi
1041	```
1042	
1043	The `$-` variable contains shell flags, and `i` means interactive. Hooks run in non-interactive shells, so the echo is skipped.
1044	
1045	When your hook returns `permissionDecision` or `additionalContext` at the top level instead of inside `hookSpecificOutput`, the JSON still parses, and Claude Code ignores the misplaced fields without reporting an error. To see which fields it ignored, start Claude Code with `claude --debug` and search the [debug log](/docs/en/hooks#debug-hooks) for `Hook JSON output had unrecognized keys`.
1046	
1047	### Debug techniques
1048	
1049	Press `Ctrl+O` to open the transcript view to check the outcome of a hook run:
1050	
1051	* **Successful run**: you see nothing, unless the hook's JSON surfaces something, such as `systemMessage` or Stop hook feedback.
1052	  * To confirm a hook ran, check for its effect, like a reformatted file, or turn on debug logging as described below and trigger the hook again
1053	* **Blocking error**: on most events you see the hook's feedback. When the hook's JSON made a blocking decision, the feedback is the reason from that decision; otherwise it is the hook's stderr. On a few events, such as `ConfigChange` and `Elicitation`, a block surfaces no message.
1054	* **Non-blocking error**: the action proceeded, and you see a `<hook name> hook error` notice with a short explanation, such as the first line of stderr prefixed with `Failed with non-blocking status code:`, or a JSON validation or parse message.
1055	
1056	Which exit-code and JSON combinations produce each outcome, including the per-event exceptions, is defined in the reference's [Exit code output](/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output) section.
1057	
1058	For full execution details including which hooks matched, their exit codes, stdout, and stderr, read the debug log. Start Claude Code with `claude --debug-file /tmp/claude.log` to write to a known path, then `tail -f /tmp/claude.log` in another terminal. If you started without that flag, run `/debug` mid-session to enable logging and find the log path.
1059	
1060	## Learn more
1061	
1062	* [Hooks reference](/docs/en/hooks): full event schemas, JSON output format, async hooks, and MCP tool hooks
1063	* [Security considerations](/docs/en/hooks#security-considerations): review before deploying hooks in shared or production environments
1064	* [Bash command validator example](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/examples/hooks/bash_command_validator_example.py): complete reference implementation
1065

Also quote exact text about whether hook config changes to settings.json are picked up by already-running sessions automatically via a file watcher, or require a new/restarted session, and whether any trust/approval step (via /hooks or otherwise) is required before an externally-edited hook actually executes for security reasons.

content.content:
# Tool Calls Covered by PreToolUse/PostToolUse Hooks

According to the documentation:

> on every tool call inside the agentic loop: `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse`, except [`EndConversation`](/docs/en/tools-reference#endconversation-tool-behavior) calls, which skip both

So PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks fire on **every tool call except EndConversation calls**.

# Hook Configuration File Changes

Regarding whether hook config changes are picked up automatically:

> Direct edits to hooks in settings files are normally picked up automatically by the file watcher.

So **yes, changes are picked up automatically** by the file watcher—no restart required for already-running sessions.

# Trust/Approval Requirements

The documentation does **not mention** any requirement for an approval step (via `/hooks` or otherwise) before an externally-edited hook executes for security reasons. The `/hooks` menu mentioned in the documentation is described as "read-only" for browsing configured hooks:

> The menu displays all five hook types... The menu is read-only: to add, modify, or remove hooks, edit the settings JSON directly or ask Claude to make the change.

There is no mention of needing to approve or trust hooks before they execute after being externally edited.

content.text:
**1. Dispara para AskUserQuestion?**
Sim. Matchers de `PreToolUse` filtram por nome da ferramenta (tabela "What the matcher filters" → `PreToolUse`: "tool name"), e `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` disparam "on every tool call inside the agentic loop... **except `EndConversation` calls, which skip both**" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md). `AskUserQuestion` não está entre as exceções documentadas — a única exceção citada na doc é `EndConversation`. Não há menção a nenhuma exceção específica para `AskUserQuestion`.

**2. Sessões já abertas pegam a mudança sem reiniciar? /hooks é obrigatório?**
Pegam automaticamente, sem precisar de `/hooks` ou restart: "If you edit settings files directly while Claude Code is running, the file watcher normally picks up hook changes automatically" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md, seção "Configure hook location"). E mais adiante: "Direct edits to hooks in settings files are normally picked up automatically by the file watcher" (troubleshooting "`/hooks` shows no hooks configured" — se não aparecer em alguns segundos, "restart your session to force a reload" como fallback).
O `/hooks` é **somente leitura** ("The `/hooks` menu is read-only. To add, modify, or remove hooks, edit your settings JSON directly or ask Claude to make the change") — serve para inspeção/verificação, não é uma revisão obrigatória/gate de segurança antes de o hook editado externamente passar a valer. A documentação não descreve nenhuma etapa de aprovação/trust separada para hooks editados fora da sessão. (A doc não distingue explicitamente app desktop vs CLI aqui — presumo mesmo comportamento de file watcher para ambos, mas isso não está dito literalmente; se quiser certeza para o desktop app especificamente, não documentado.)

**3. Exit code 2 bloqueia com stderr? Alternativa JSON `permissionDecision: "deny"`?**
Sim, ambos suportados em `PreToolUse`:
- Exit 2: "Exit 2: Claude Code blocks the action. Write a reason to stderr... For `PreToolUse` this feeds it to Claude as feedback so it can adjust" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md, seção "Hook output").
- JSON: 
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "..."
  }
}
```
"With `\"deny\"`, Claude Code cancels the tool call and feeds `permissionDecisionReason` back to Claude." A doc recomenda escolher uma abordagem por hook: "Use exit 2 to block with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON for structured control. Choose one approach per hook."

Fontes: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md e https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (Hooks reference).
